title: Energy Pouches: Caffeine Pouches - Tobacco Insider
abstract:
When we feel the need for a boost, we traditionally resort to nicotine and caffeine as an “every day use” booster – mostly consumed in the form of cigarettes and drinks, respectively. **Caffeine** is a stimulant that impacts the brain and central nervous system to keep us awake. Meanwhile, nicotine is a stimulant that results in dopamine release, boosting our vigilance. Although the two substances produce different reactions in the body, they are both effective in “waking us up”.  
Delivery of nicotine to the human body is being revolutionized with the emergence of the convenient pouch format. Smokers are increasingly replacing their traditional tobacco products, cigarettes or moist smokeless tobacco, with nicotine pouches in the US and elsewhere. Can the delivery of caffeine (or other revitalizing substances) be revolutionized by the same product concept? Can the pouch format help consumers move forward from traditional caffeine products, coffee or energy drinks, to a more convenient & effective solution? Entrepreneurs all around the world are testing whether **caffeine pouches** could answer these questions. But, first of all, what is a caffeine pouch?
A caffeine pouch is a small, porous (semi-permeable) sack containing a revitalizing ingredient (“natural energy booster”), caffeine in most cases (guarana, green tea or black tea more rarely). The pouch may also contain certain vitamins (B5, B6, B12, C), minerals or antioxidants, and come in different flavors, such as mint, cinnamon, caramel, licorice, citrus, orange or berry. Caffeine pouches claim to increase our energy, thereby combating fatigue and improving vitality. In some cases, caffeine pouches are even marketed as a way to curb nicotine craving with the potential to be an exit product from nicotine pouch consumption and dependency.  
**Attention:** Caffeine pouches are not coffee pouches! Coffee pouches are coffee-flavored nicotine pouches (such as ZYN, on! and VELO). They taste like coffee and contain nicotine. Meanwhile, caffeine pouches are energy pouches without nicotine (such as mojo and Grinds). Their primary purpose is to give the user an energy boost. Rather than a coffee flavor, caffeine pouches usually have sweet or fruity flavors. And, yes, it is theorically possible to have a coffee-flavored, caffeinated nicotine pouch. But what is the point with that?
Caffeine pouches are typically marketed in a can of 20 with each pouch weighing 0.5 to 1 gram and lasting for 30 minutes or so. Depending on the market and brand, a can of 20 pouches usually costs between $4 to $12. Users place the caffeine pouches in their mouth, between the cheek / lips and gums and the ingredients in the pouch are absorbed through the mouth tissues with the saliva facilitating a suitable, moist environment. It is claimed that the absorption is quicker and the time-to-kick-in (i.e. time course of the ingredient action) is shorter than energy drinks.  
**Are caffeine pouches the next Big Thing?**  
Possibly. For instance, at the 2024 CAGNY Conference, Marlboro-owner, Altria defined non-nicotine adjacencies as a $100Bn total addressable market in the US – including the products with no age-restricted ingredients (i.e. no nicotine or THC). Based on the findings of their large-scale research, Altria stated that:  
– consumers increasingly want to improve their physical and emotional state  
– consumers are specifically looking to “elevate their everyday” through moments of enhanced energy, focus, stress relief and relaxation  
– nearly 60% of adults are struggling to find effective solutions for stress and relaxation, and more than 40% are seeking better options to elevate their energy (i.e. the focus area of caffeine pouches).
